questions.question: Explain how plants make their food.
questions.expected_answer: Plants make their food in their leaves. The green leaves catch energy from sunlight and use it to turn water from the roots and a gas from the air into food. While doing this, they give off oxygen.

questions.question: Name three plant parts where food is stored, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: seeds, like maize, wheat or beans; roots, like carrots or sweet potatoes; underground stems, like potatoes; stems, like sugar cane; leaves, like cabbage or spinach; fruits, like mangoes or oranges.

questions.question: Explain why we can say that the energy in a beef stew came from the Sun.
questions.expected_answer: The beef came from cattle. The cattle got their energy by eating grass. The grass made its food using energy from sunlight. So the energy passed from the Sun to the grass, to the cattle, and then to us.
